title: Best AI for coding? Budget roughly 20€ per month
author: Brief-Chance542
selftext:
Hey guys! Unity Dev here. Was wondering which AI is best and most affordable at this current date? 

Right now I'm using Gemini with a 20€ per month plan, but I'm not that happy as with bugfixing, Gemini is often not able to find the bug sources. 

20€ or $20 USD is also roughly my monthly budget at the moment since I'm not yet making money from my games. I work on my game 5 to 9 hours per day. I **only** need it for coding! So no 3D assets or visuals. I also don't care weather it's in engine (Unity) or in my IDE or if I copy-paste my scripts to a website (as I'm doing now). I'm working on a quite complex system with lots of cutsom physics and stuff. For personal reasons, I'd like to stay away from open AI.

Thankful for any pointers or ideas!

comments.author: TheCelestialBubble
comments.body:
Right, a lot of these comments in the post have no nuance whatsoever and clearly just stans. I have had great personal experience using Claude Opus 5.5 for coding and I think it's probably the best, but realistically if it's
 just code you need it for, and you are very hands on, any of the frontier should be fine. You say you Gemini is not working well, but unless you're referring to pre-4 Gemini, I dont fully understand how. It should be more than capable of coding C#. I can only imagine the issue is your prompting or your method. If you have a bug with the visual aspect of physics and can't explain it well, all models are likely to struggle, at least in my experience (and Claude has the worst visual acuity by quite a margin I'd argue; obv it can read numbers but this only works so well). And copy pasting code is... Odd. I would really implore you to just add Gemini to your vscode or whatever and point it at your repo.

I don't really know the limits of Gemini and Chatgpt well, but Claude feels as though it's recently shrank it's max plans too...

Also ate up my daily usage limit within just 3 messages, but the bug was gone. Now Argon sadly is no longer included in my plan, hence the search for a different service that fits my situation and budget. Yes, I agree that copy pasting is sub optimal, I am kinda hesitant of adding AI directly to my IDE or Unity, as I'm afraid of it destroying something in the background that I notice too late, copy-pasting feels... saver? Also like my game is still *my* game. Just a personal thing. With claude, many here were pointing out that with $20 USD one can't get very far

replies.author: TheCelestialBubble
replies.body: So! 3.1 was lightyears behind the rest and if you posted this a month ago I would never recommend Gemini, and 100% would've agreed with your assessment. I believe hydrogen should be in your plan tho and should be more than capable. Argon is like Fable, or Opus (I can't remember the noble gases!) for Claude I think, but was their only 4 model so you didn't have much choice at the time. That being said, their new lineup is much stronger than prior and now offers different levels like gpt and Claude. I would be very tempted to give them another month. This is just my opinion but if you have really heavy physics I don't think it's feasible to just copy paste. You may be missing context in what you're giving them and they can't rjn full game level scripts (in app) to test for them self. Often for physics in a 2d game of mine for examples, Claude will run 10s of simulations in application to test what is actually happening. However, I completely understand the problem about giving up agency and respect it very much, it's just... Difficult with what you want I think. I also think the days of them destroying random things is much less likely nowadays. They will very rarely strya off task and if you give them permissions for a specific directory, they are unlikely to go outside of that.

comments.author: RemarkableWish2508
comments.body:
> 5 to 9 hours per day

> don't care [...] if I copy-paste my scripts to a website (as I'm doing now)

> I'm working on a quite complex system

No. Stop. Without some development methodology, you're just wasting time and money, no amount of AI will fix that.

If you are working in complex shit, you *need* an IDE/Agent approach, and you *need* to organize your stuff in requirements, success conditions, unit tests, integration tests, QA, support, etc.

Doesn't matter how much you want to put in those, whether you want to run a strict pipeline or a loose one; putting "zero" or not being aware of it, is not going to cut it to get an AI deal with complex things.

comments.author: Maksim_Volganin_11
comments.body:
For a €20/$20 budget—especially since you want to avoid OpenAI and are dealing with complex custom physics—
Claude Pro (or using Claude inside 
Cursor) is widely considered the strongest option for pure coding and architecture right now. It tends to hold context much better than Gemini when tracking down tricky bug sources across multiple scripts.
That said, how you prompt and structure your code makes a huge difference regardless of the model. I actually build small web game prototypes using just the 
free Google AI chat on the main search page, and it gets me surprisingly far because of two habits:
Keep scripts super modular and compact. Small, isolated files mean the AI doesn't drown in context, and copy-pasting logs or snippets stays fast and clean.
Break the "bug-fixing loop" with forced lateral thinking. Even the best models get stuck repeating the same broken fix when you paste console error logs. Whenever the chat starts looping, I tell it: 
"Give me 12 different ways to solve this problem, ranging from the most cutting-edge/standard approaches to the most unorthodox or extraordinary ones." That almost always forces it out of the rut and surfaces the actual root cause.
If you switch to Claude at $20/mo and pair it with small modular scripts + the "12 approaches" prompt whenever it gets stuck, you’ll probably see a massive jump in debugging speed.
